column1: for the invention and development of optical lattice clocks, enabling time and frequency measurements at unprecedented precision — Jun Ye, Hidetoshi Katori
for the theoretical prediction and experimental realization of negative index metamaterials — John B. Pendry, David R. Smith, Eli Yablonovitch
for the theoretical prediction and experimental discovery of topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect — Eugene J. Mele, Charles L. Kane, Laurens W. Molenkamp
for theoretical proposals and experimental realizations of quantum simulators using ultracold atoms in optical lattices — Immanuel Bloch, J. Ignacio Cirac, Peter Zoller
for the discovery of topological and geometric phases in quantum systems — Michael V. Berry, Yakir Aharonov

for the theoretical prediction and experimental discovery of correlated insulator behavior and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene — Pablo Jarillo-Herrero, Allan H. MacDonald, Rafi Bistritzer
for foundational discoveries in quantum information science, including quantum cryptography and quantum algorithms — Charles H. Bennett, Gilles Brassard, Peter W. Shor
for advancing the understanding of the surprising properties of two-dimensional electron systems in strong magnetic fields — Mordehai Heiblum, Jainendra K. Jain, James P. Eisenstein
for their studies of stellar explosions and the origin of the elements — Ken'ichi Nomoto, Stanford Woosley

for the development of highly efficient organic light-emitting diodes based on phosphorescent and thermally activated delayed fluorescence emitters — Chihaya Adachi, Mark E. Thompson, Stephen R. Forrest
for pioneering contributions to neutrino astronomy, in particular the discovery of high-energy cosmic neutrinos — Francis Halzen, Albrecht Karle, Naoko Kurahashi Neilson
for pioneering theoretical studies of fluctuations in the cosmic microwave background — George Efstathiou, John Richard Bond
for the discovery of quantum error correction and fault-tolerant quantum computation — John Preskill, Peter W. Shor, Alexei Y. Kitaev
for the invention of the quantum cascade laser — Federico Capasso, Alfred Y. Cho, Jérôme Faist
for the formulation of the hydrodynamic theories of active matter and flocking — John Toner, Sriram Ramaswamy, Yuhai Tu
for the experimental discovery of the quantum anomalous Hall effect — Qikun Xue
for the invention of aberration-corrected electron optics, enabling electron microscopy with sub-ångström resolution — Maximilian Haider, Knut Urban, Ondrej L. Krivanek
for numerical simulations that established the cold dark matter model of the formation of cosmic structure — Simon White, Carlos Frenk, Marc Davis

for the discovery of fluctuation theorems and exact nonequilibrium work relations that extend thermodynamics to small systems far from equilibrium — Christopher Jarzynski, Denis J. Evans, Gavin E. Crooks
for the detection and theoretical study of the atmospheres of exoplanets through their transits — David Charbonneau, Sara Seager
for the observation of the shadow of a black hole by event-horizon-scale radio interferometry — Heino Falcke, Sheperd S. Doeleman, Katherine L. Bouman
for the theory of multiferroic materials, in which magnetic and ferroelectric order coexist — Nicola A. Spaldin
for the discovery of magnetic skyrmion lattices and topological spin textures in chiral magnets — Christian Pfleiderer, Yoshinori Tokura, Naoto Nagaosa
for theoretical discoveries of quantum spin liquids and exactly solvable models of topological order — Alexei Y. Kitaev, Patrick A. Lee
for the invention of atomic force microscopy — Christoph Gerber, Gerd Binnig
for fundamental contributions to high-energy astrophysics, galaxies and structure formation, and cosmology — Martin Rees
for the theoretical formulation of cosmic inflation and the prediction of the quantum origin of cosmological structure — Alan H. Guth, Andrei Linde, Viatcheslav Mukhanov
for the proposal of quantum computation with electron spins in semiconductor quantum dots — Daniel Loss, David DiVincenzo
for the development of wavelet theory and multiresolution signal analysis — Yves Meyer, Stéphane Mallat, Ingrid Daubechies
for the first coherent control of a superconducting quantum bit — Yasunobu Nakamura
